rows.comment: Passive and slightly roundabout. Say what the band did record and what it lacked.
lineComments: Passive voice; name the two data types directly.
rows.replacement: 'The band recorded heart rate but no motion data.'

rows.comment: Em dash and a piled-up clause. Split into two sentences saying what the import holds and what is missing.
lineComments: Em dash; "carries the night only" is a flourish for "contains only the night".
Repeats "nothing was recorded" and ties it to a second clause with "and there is".
Say plainly there are no raw records to compute from.
rows.replacement:
'This day comes from an imported export, which holds the night only. '
'The app has no waking-day data and no raw records to compute it from.'

rows.comment: Em dash and a roundabout "has not produced any activity to read". State that no activity data has arrived.
lineComments: Second half only restates the first.
rows.replacement: 'No activity data has reached the app for today yet.'

rows.comment: "Has no X behind it" is a figure of speech. Say the value was not recorded.
lineComments: Replace the metaphor with a direct statement.
rows.replacement: 'That night has no total sleep time recorded.'

rows.comment: "Behind it" is a figure of speech. Say the value was not recorded.
lineComments: Replace the metaphor with a direct statement.
rows.replacement: 'That night has no wake time recorded.'

rows.comment: "Behind it" is a figure of speech. Say the value was not recorded.

rows.replacement: 'That night has no sleep efficiency recorded.'

rows.comment: Convoluted; "ceiling" is a metaphor for maximum heart rate. Name it.
lineComments: "Held a high enough heart rate through a hard effort" is hard to parse.
"Measure a ceiling from" dangles; say maximum heart rate.
rows.replacement:
'Your heart rate has not yet stayed high enough during a hard effort '
'to measure your maximum.'

rows.comment: Contrast with an effort nobody called maximal ("rather than as your ceiling") and an em dash. State what the app does with the value.
lineComments: "Sits well below what your age predicts" is vague; say it is below the age-based estimate.
"Rather than" rebuts a reading the user never made.
The zone behaviour is the useful fact; state it directly.
rows.replacement:
'Your highest recorded heart rate is well below the age-based estimate, '
'so the app treats it as a submaximal effort. '
'Zones use the age estimate until the band records a harder effort.'

rows.comment: "Behind the reserve" is figurative. Say what the reserve needs.
lineComments: Name the requirement: more nights of resting heart rate.
rows.replacement: 'Heart rate reserve needs more nights of resting heart rate.'

rows.comment: "Anchor" is jargon and "measured reserve" is undefined. Say there is no heart rate reserve to plot.
lineComments: "No measured reserve anchor" is stacked jargon.
"Plot a distribution against" is awkward; say what is not shown.
rows.replacement:
'You set your zones manually, so there is no heart rate reserve '
'to plot a distribution against.'

rows.comment: "Rather than noise" rebuts something nobody claimed. State the shortfall.
lineComments: Drop the contrast; say too few sessions to show a pattern.
rows.replacement: 'Too few recorded sessions to show a pattern.'

rows.comment: Mixes tense ("were" vs "needs") and reads clumsily. Present tense, both counts kept.
lineComments: Keep $why and both interpolations; fix tense and structure.
rows.replacement: '$why The app has ${c[1]} and needs ${c[2]}.'

rows.comment: "Rather than guessed" rebuts nothing the reader raised. Keep the reason (per-strap calibration, no strap ID) and the withholding.
lineComments: "Stamped with which strap made them" is roundabout; say recordings carry no strap ID.
Calibration reason is useful; the contrast clause that follows is not.
"Rather than guessed" is a flourish; the value is simply withheld.
rows.replacement:
'These recordings do not say which strap made them. '
'This number needs a per-strap calibration, so the app withholds it.'
